svg.title: DRAFT: Evidence fork, choose an observation before repairing a Linux service
svg.desc: Illustrative, non-interactive concept. One workstation, studio-17, has an old service report and no fresh inventory. The operator compares a changed service against stopped reporting without claiming either explanation is true. Both branches identify evidence needed to distinguish them. The selected next action requests one inventory refresh, not a restart or policy change. Acceptance does not resolve the question; a new relevant report is required. Missing, collection-error and ambiguous-action outcomes remain unresolved. Saving questions and linking evidence are proposed backend work.

g.text: LINDM / CONCEPT 01 / DRAFT OWNER SELECTION / ILLUSTRATIVE DATA
What would tell us whether to intervene?
studio-17 · One unresolved question · No repair requested
Is the printing service still stopped?
Last service report: stopped, yesterday 16:20. Current state: unknown.
Possibility A: the service is still stopped
Would support it
A fresh service observation still reports stopped.
Would not establish it
A missing report or an accepted refresh request.
Operator-authored question, not an automatic diagnosis
Possibility B: our evidence stopped arriving
Would support it
Fresh inventory arrives but service evidence does not.
Still uncertain
A collection error does not prove a transport fault.
Both explanations may be incomplete
Choose the next observation
Refresh inventory for studio-17
Existing action. Requests collection only; does not restart printing or change policy.
Unknown stays unknown until relevant evidence arrives
If accepted: wait for the new report. If collection fails: show the reported error.
If submission is ambiguous: recover the same request, do not issue a second refresh.
Review one inventory request
Leave question unresolved
PROPOSED: saved questions + evidence links. Static sketch: controls are not interactive.
